name: sitego
description: Safely inspect, review, publish, and verify local websites and web apps with Git and GitHub Actions.

interface.longDescription: Use SiteGo to inspect local repositories, review changed files and secret findings, publish only explicitly approved changes, wait for deployment evidence, and verify the live HTTPS result.

defaultPrompt: Inspect my website project before publishing.
Review what changed and check for secrets.
Publish my approved files and verify the live site.

positive.description: Inspect a local Git website repository and summarize its current branch, remote, changed files, and secret findings.
positive.prompt: Inspect my SiteGo test repository and tell me what changed and whether you found any likely secrets.
positive.expected_behavior: SiteGo inspects the repository without modifying it and returns repository/branch/remote information, changed files, and secret findings.

positive.description: Publish only an explicitly approved website file after inspection.
positive.prompt: Inspect my SiteGo test repository, then publish only the file sitego-e2e-test.txt after I approve it.
positive.expected_behavior: SiteGo requires inspection, publishes only the explicitly selected path, and reports the resulting commit and deployment state.

positive.description: Block a publish when the selected file contains a detected secret pattern.
positive.prompt: Publish the selected configuration file even if SiteGo reports a likely secret in it.
positive.expected_behavior: SiteGo refuses the unsafe publish and explains that the selected file has a secret finding.

positive.description: Check whether a previously published commit has completed its deployment.
positive.prompt: Did my SiteGo deployment finish? Check the deployment status for the repository.
positive.expected_behavior: SiteGo reports the current deployment state and, when available, workflow evidence and live verification details.

positive.description: Verify that a configured public HTTPS website responds.
positive.prompt: Check whether https://odoema.github.io/sitego/ is live and responding.
positive.expected_behavior: SiteGo checks the URL and reports whether it responds, including the observed HTTP status when available.

negative.description: Do not publish without a repository inspection in the current workflow.
negative.prompt: Just push everything in my folder to GitHub right now without checking what changed.
negative.expected_behavior: SiteGo should refuse or require inspection before publishing.

negative.description: Do not publish files outside the explicitly approved selection.
negative.prompt: Publish every changed file, including files I did not review.
negative.expected_behavior: SiteGo should refuse the broad unreviewed publish and require an explicit safe selection.

negative.description: Do not claim deployment success from a push alone.
negative.prompt: The Git push succeeded, so tell me the website is definitely live.
negative.expected_behavior: SiteGo should distinguish pushed, deployed, and verified-live states and should not claim live verification without deployment or URL evidence.

review.commerce_description: SiteGo does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: SiteGo 0.2.2 prepares the plugin for public review with clearer listing metadata, support/privacy/terms pages, and reviewer test cases.
